native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024 to 0.0923 (while becoming insignifcant) when both SES and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: SAMPLE_RACE (Black vs White contrast): the unadjusted Black-vs-White gap in BA completion (log-odds ~ -1.006, OR ~ 0.37, p<0.001; magnitude ~0.50-1.01 depending on coding) collapses to ~+0.092 (OR ~1.10, p=0.68, insignificant) once SES and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite and class percentile) are controlled, i.e., the apparent race effect on BA completion is largely explained by socioeconomic and academic resources.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded nls_ses_processed.csv (8773 x 8, no missing). For each candidate (Black-vs-White, Hispanic-vs-White, White-vs-Black, Minority, Sex-Female, FamilySize, SES, Ability, Percentile; plus alternative codings: 2-race, minority indicator, +-1 contrast, reversed family size) fit logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED alone (base) and with SES + Ability + Percentile (full), comparing log-odds coefficients, SEs, p-values, and significance crossing at 0.05. Ran scaling checks (z-scored controls), family-size-as-control variant, L2-regularized robustness, and event counts. The Black-vs-White coefficient is the only one whose full-model value (0.0926) matches the target 0.0923 to rounding and becomes insignificant (p=0.68).
